prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Havenline game-art connection reference sheet, landscape, four large coherent panels.
Primary request: Render the COMPLETE storage-house conveyor connection upgrade in the newly owner-approved LOW conveyor family. This is a new concept sheet using exact supplied references; do not reproduce the old tall-legged conveyor kit.
Input images, in order: 1 is the APPROVED conveyor R1, the authority for low solid orange housings, thick yellow upper rims, closely spaced black cylindrical rollers, silver bridge plates and blue machinery/base. Preserve its scale and material language. 2 is the EXISTING storage-house design and FOUR PORTS/local transfer topology to preserve, not its old conveyor style. 3 is APPROVED core R4, the authority for unchanged Character1 and SMALL ordinary resource-unit sizes. Big stockpiles are many small units, not huge individual items.
Visual style: polished rounded high-quality 3D mobile-game assets, clean warm peach studio floor/background, soft contact shadows, orange/blue/timber building materials, restrained snow only on roof/cold edges. No photorealism, no watermark. Wide landscape sheet with thin panel divisions, simple dark headings and ample room for visible connections. Show real surfaces, not a flowchart.
Header exactly: "HAVENLINE / STORAGE CONNECTIONS".
TOP LEFT: "UTILITY IN / OUT". Three-quarter FRONT-LEFT exterior of the same recognizable blue storage house: peaked blue snowy roof, orange timber trim and crate emblem, original front double blue sliding doors and accessible apron, retained high left window. Two separate LOW ports under that window, clearly marked IN and OUT. Orange/yellow low roller modules meet those ports through supported silver bridge plates; receiving lane inward, dispatch lane outward. Small plank bundles and stone/block units fit easily on the surfaces. Keep the front doorway and apron completely clear. Put unchanged Character1 standing beside the front approach at natural size as the scale anchor, no tools or new uniform.
TOP RIGHT: "PREPARED FOOD IN / OUT". Rear-right exterior of the SAME house, retaining round rear vent and original right-side fuel hatch. Exactly two rear food sleeves at the prepared-food shelf height, clearly labeled IN and OUT, BELOW the vent and ABOVE the closed raw-food cabinets. The house has two separate food lines. Each rises from the approved low orange roller housings to the higher food port through a fully supported orange enclosed inclined height adapter and silver mating plate. No floating shelf, open gap, thin tall legs, or belt cutting through a wall. Several small prepared-food units show direction. Right fuel hatch and rear service path remain accessible.
BOTTOM LEFT: "UTILITY TRAY / LIFT". Accurate cutaway of the same LEFT ports. Show separate low receiving and dispatch landings, a compact indexed local lifting tray reaching two distinct shelves labeled TIMBER and MINERALS. Small same-size plank bundles and mineral units occupy their correct shelves. The lift has a real guide and platform, and local supported transfer surfaces connect both ports. No mixed endless loop, no invisible transport, no front door obstruction.
BOTTOM RIGHT: "FOOD SHELF SHUTTLE". Accurate interior cutaway of the SAME rear shelf-level IN/OUT sleeves. One short horizontal local shuttle physically carries small prepared-food portions between the two sleeves and shelf stock. Both raw-food cabinets remain closed below and the round vent remains above. Match exterior physical port sides correctly when looking from inside: do not reverse IN and OUT on the same opening. Show a small low-capacity stock row and an input hold gate when receiving area is full. Keep a clear center walking aisle.
Hard constraints: preserve storage-house identity and four distinct typed ports; the low housing/black roller/yellow rim family from image1 replaces all old open tall-legged belt geometry in image2. Raised sleeves require supported height adapters. Unchanged C1 and selected R4 small units. No register, clerk, new factory, long road, universal mixed-food/mineral belt, random extra ports, food on utility shelves, or currency conveyor. This is static design art, not proof of working animation.
